name: Inequality
shortcutSummary: Chain the inequalities. If A > B and B > C, then A > C (transitive). For coded inequality, first decode the symbols, then chain. No conclusion can be drawn if the chain breaks (e.g., A > B and C > B gives no relation between A and C).
conceptExplanation:
Inequality questions involve comparing values using symbols (>, <, =, ≥, ≤). You must determine whether given conclusions follow from the inequality chain.

Types: Direct inequality (standard symbols) and Coded inequality (symbols like @, #, $ represent comparison operators).

subtopics.name: Inequality — Core Concepts
subtopics.explanation:
Inequality questions involve comparing values using symbols (>, <, =, ≥, ≤). You must determine whether given conclusions follow from the inequality chain.

Types: Direct inequality (standard symbols) and Coded inequality (symbols like @, #, $ represent comparison operators).
shortcuts: Chain Method: Write all inequalities in a single chain. If the chain connects the two variables, you can conclude.
Either-Or Rule: If exactly one of two complementary conclusions must be true, "Either I or II follows."
Decode First: For coded inequality, build a legend of what each symbol means before solving.

practiceQuestions.questionText:
Statements: T > R ≥ U = S > Q
Conclusions:
I. T > U
II. S > Q
options: Only conclusion II follows
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
Both conclusion I and II follow
Only conclusion I follows
practiceQuestions.hint: Check the operator priority hierarchy: > overrides ≥ which overrides =.
practiceQuestions.explanation: From T > R ≥ U, the common priority operator is ">", so T > U is definitely true. From S > Q, conclusion II is definitely true. Both conclusions follow.
practiceQuestions.solutionSteps:
Step 1: Check the chain of operators between the two variables in Conclusion I.
Step 2: Check the chain of operators between the two variables in Conclusion II.
Step 3: If opposite signs (e.g. > and <) appear anywhere between them, no definite conclusion can be drawn.
Step 4: Result is Both conclusion I and II follow.

practiceQuestions.questionText:
In the following question, the symbols are used as follows:
P @ Q means P is greater than Q (>)
P # Q means P is greater than or equal to Q (≥)
P $ Q means P is equal to Q (=)
P % Q means P is less than or equal to Q (≤)
P * Q means P is less than Q (<)

Statements: Q @ P, P # S, S $ U
Conclusions:
I. Q @ U
II. P $ U
options: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
Only conclusion I follows
Either conclusion I or II follows
Only conclusion II follows
practiceQuestions.hint: Decode the coded symbols into standard mathematical operators (> , ≥ , = , ≤ , <) before evaluating.
practiceQuestions.explanation: Decoding the statements: Q > P ≥ S = U. Conclusion I: Q > U (True, as ">" is the highest priority operator in the chain). Conclusion II: P = U (False, as P ≥ U does not guarantee equality). Therefore, only conclusion I follows.
practiceQuestions.solutionSteps:
Step 1: Replace coded symbols with standard inequality signs.
Step 2: Chain: Q > P ≥ S = U.
Step 3: Evaluate Conclusion I (Q > U) -> Definite True.
Step 4: Evaluate Conclusion II (P = U) -> Only possible, not definite.
